headline: Greenland opposition party wants a referendum on the US defence deal
headline_short: Greenland's parliament debates the US deal
deck: Parliament held the first reading on Monday; the governing coalition holds 19 of its 31 seats.
standard: Greenland's parliament, Inatsisartut, held the first reading of the new security and defence agreement with the United States and Denmark on Monday and sent it to a second reading, which has no date yet. The vote comes only at the third reading. The governing coalition holds 19 of the 31 seats.

Pele Broberg, leader of Naleraq, an opposition party, wants the deal put to a referendum. He said it 'turns our country's importance into rights for the United States' without a matching economic return for Greenlanders. According to KNR, a Greenlandic news outlet, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Greenland's head of government, replied that the US had put no 'offers of money on the table'.
The deal was signed on 22 September. It extends one from 1951 and lets the US set up two more military bases.
short: Greenland's parliament held the first reading of the new defence agreement with the United States and Denmark on Monday. Naleraq, an opposition party, wants it put to a referendum, but the governing coalition holds 19 of the 31 seats.
